title: Engineers work weekdays
author: agam
hypothesis: Hacker News runs on the work week: a weekday carries well over 30% more activity than a weekend day.
expect: If true, average daily items on Mon-Fri should be at least 1.3x the average on Sat-Sun.
caveats: Weekdays are UTC. Someone posting Friday night in Asia counts as Friday.
Window is 11 weeks (Jul 22 - Oct 8 2026), so one holiday can move the result.
Counts all items, comments included.

title: HN never sleeps
author: agam
hypothesis: Software engineers are night owls: the quiet hours (00-05 UTC) are about as busy as the peak hours (13-18 UTC).
expect: If true, average hourly items at 00-05 UTC should be within 10% of 13-18 UTC (ratio between 0.9 and 1.1).
caveats: HN is global. 00-05 UTC is daytime in Asia and evening in the Americas, so this tests the crowd, not one person.
Counts all items, comments included.

title: Monday rush
author: agam
hypothesis: Everyone comes back to the keyboard on Monday: it is the busiest day of the week.
expect: If true, average items on Mondays should be at least 1.15x the average of the other six days (1.10x counts as weak).
caveats: Weekdays are UTC.
11-week window: about 11 Mondays, so one odd Monday matters.
Comparing against the other six days includes the quiet weekend, which flatters Monday.

title: Friday slump
author: agam
hypothesis: Friday is when the work week winds down: it is quieter than the middle of the week.
expect: If true, average items on Fridays should be at most 0.85x the Tue-Thu average (0.95x counts as weak).
caveats: Weekdays are UTC. Friday evening in the Americas is already Saturday UTC, which cuts Friday and lifts Saturday.
11-week window.

title: Early birds
author: agam
hypothesis: The HN crowd is made of morning people: early hours (06-09 UTC) are at least as busy as the evening (18-21 UTC).
expect: If true, average hourly items at 06-09 UTC should be at least 1.1x the 18-21 UTC average.
caveats: HN is global, so UTC hours mix time zones. This tests the crowd, not individuals.
Counts all items, comments included.

title: Quiet days pay the same
author: agam
hypothesis: Weekends have fewer posts but the same appetite: a weekend day earns at least 90% of the points a weekday does.
expect: If true, average points per day on Sat-Sun should be at least 0.9x the Mon-Fri average (below 0.8x refutes it).
caveats: Points are summed over items that have a score (stories), so this is points per day, not per post.
Weekdays are UTC. 11-week window.

title: Saturday is for side projects
author: agam
hypothesis: Saturday is the day people ship and share personal projects: it is busier than Sunday.
expect: If true, average items on Saturdays should be at least 1.1x Sundays (below 0.9x refutes it).
caveats: Weekdays are UTC. Late Friday in the Americas lands on Saturday UTC.
Counts all items, not only Show HN. A Show HN check would need a title-based summary.
11-week window.

title: The midweek peak
author: agam
hypothesis: Activity builds to a midweek peak: Tuesday to Thursday beat Monday and Friday.
expect: If true, average items Tue-Thu should be at least 1.05x the Mon and Fri average (1.15x counts as strong, below 0.97x refutes it).
caveats: Weekdays are UTC.
The gap is small, so 11 weeks is thin evidence.

title: The new systems languages rise
author: agam
hypothesis: Rust and Zig are gaining ground on HN: their share of story titles keeps climbing.
expect: If true, the share of stories with Rust, Zig, rustc or cargo in the title should be at least 1.3x higher in the latest 4 full weeks than in the first 4 (1.1x counts as weak, below 0.9x refutes it).
caveats: Title matching only: a story about Rust that never says Rust is missed, and cargo can mean freight.
Only complete Monday-start UTC weeks in the window are used; the window is about 10 weeks, so this is a short trend.
Stories only, not comments.

title: Deep tech punches above its weight
author: agam
hypothesis: Deep-tech topics (quantum, fusion, photonics, chips, batteries, gene editing) earn clearly more HN attention per story than the rest.
expect: If true, deep-tech stories should average at least 1.3x the points per story of all other stories, week by week on average (1.1x counts as weak, below 0.9x refutes it).
caveats: This tests traction on HN, not lead time over the mainstream. Ten weeks cannot show who was early.
Points are skewed: one hit story can move a week. Weekly means are shown, not medians.
Topic list is title keywords chosen in advance (scripts/terms.py); other deep-tech stories are missed.

title: Weird goes big
author: agam
hypothesis: Strange, old and mysterious stories travel further than the average story.
expect: If true, stories with words like weird, mystery, ancient, abandoned or forgotten in the title should average at least 1.3x the points per story of all other stories (1.1x counts as weak, below 0.9x refutes it).
caveats: Word list was fixed in advance (scripts/terms.py) and is a rough stand-in for weird.
Points are skewed: one hit story can move a week.
